newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS-EU asks US for more economic consultation.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-EU asks US for more economic consultation.

text.p: The European Commission told the United States on Tuesday it wanted to develop closer consultations in monetary and economic matters.
A Commission spokesman said the request was made by European Economic Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy during a meeting with U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright.
He said de Silguy had particularly requested more consultation over macro-economic issues.
The spokesman said Albright had replied that she hoped this could be discussed in more depth at the U.S.-European Union summit in May in the Netherlands.
Commission officials said the desire for closer cooperation with the United States stemmed largely from a consideration of the external implications of a common European currency.
To the extent such a currency alters the nature of the world's monetary system, there might be a greater incentive for Washington to participate in closer coordination of policies.
As an example, officials pointed to the fact that 33 percent of world trade is currently denominated in European currencies. The EU also accounts for 38 percent of world exports and imports.
By contrast, the United States accounts for only 12 percent of world trade, but 48 percent of such trade is invoiced in dollars.
A single European currency might alter the balance of this relationship and give the EU a more influential role in policy consultations, officials added.

De Silguy is scheduled to visit a wide range of American financial institutions and investors in April on a trip designed to inform them on recent developments on the progress to economic and monetary union. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
